correctness.rationale: For every n>=0 and each listed forbidden triple, the Type-A edge normal form uniquely identifies the alternating difference interval; both phases avoid 001 exactly when a common prefix is empty or ends in 1 and a common suffix does not start 01. Their length series are P=1/(1-z-z^2) and S=(1+z)/(1-z-z^2). Every possible long-edge triangle cut has exactly one admissible splice, yielding E=P*S*z^2/(1-z), T=P*S*z^4/(1-z)^2. The factor orbit under reversal/complement covers all four triples. Both independent programs passed direct deck computations through n=12, explicit interval enumeration through n=10, and exact rational coefficient checks through n=32. Finite checks corroborate the structural proof and are not treated as an all-length proof.

value.rationale: The two-read reconstruction graph is a natural finite-blocklength ambiguity invariant. Exact all-length counts of competing source pairs and mutual ambiguity triples for an asymmetric, minimal-length forbidden local motif explain one-splice survival, yield a Fibonacci-modulated density, and establish a cumulative edge–triangle law with limiting mean three triangles per edge. This measures a structural channel-reconstruction gap rather than merely recomputing a familiar unrestricted count; no code-capacity claim is made.
